title: Ocean current length evidence and rank eligibility
rule: Only published approximate along-current or system-length estimates admitted as established flows are ordered. Proposed continuity hypotheses, sampled reaches, derived or published lower bounds, and unknown lengths are unranked. Estimates with different system boundaries are not precise head-to-head measurements.

status_definitions.published_estimate: Published approximate along-current or current-system length admitted to the source-set ranking; system boundaries still differ.
status_definitions.derived_lower_bound: OSW conservative geometric floor from published extent points or latitude span; not a measured flow path.
status_definitions.published_lower_bound: Source states a lower limit for the named current; not a comparable whole-current estimate.
status_definitions.proposed_system_length: Published proposed continuity or system extent; hypothesis not admitted as established whole-current length.
status_definitions.sampled_reach_only: A survey sampled part of the flow; its reach does not set the full length.
status_definitions.section_only: A cross-stream section or transport observation locates the flow but supplies no along-current length.
status_definitions.no_numeric_length: No numeric along-current length or bound admitted in the current source set.

entries.name: Antarctic Circumpolar Current
entries.scope: Approximate circumpolar path; source calls it the longest wind-driven current.
entries.length_source_locator: Section 1 Introduction, opening sentence (approximately 25,000 km)

source_reported_length_variants.scope: NASA/JPL's 2019 overview says the Antarctic Circumpolar Current spans about 13,000 miles (21,000 km). It does not specify a reference streamline or contour, so this alternate whole-current approximation is retained separately from the ranked 25,000 km research estimate.
source_reported_length_variants.source_locator: NASA/JPL article, paragraph beginning The Antarctic Circumpolar Current flows in a loop (13,000 miles / 21,000 km)

entries.name: Antarctic Coastal Current (East Wind Drift)
entries.scope: The East Wind Drift is westward near the Antarctic coast. Its continuity and start/end limits vary by sector; the four published map arrows do not supply a measured centerline or comparable whole-current length.

entries.name: California Current
entries.scope: Approximate California Current System extent from Baja California Sur to northern Vancouver Island; not a measured California Current core axis.
entries.length_source_locator: PDF page 3, background box under California Current (California Current System extends 3,000 km)

entries.name: Gulf Stream System
entries.scope: NOAA's glossary defines a continuous system comprising the Florida Current, Gulf Stream, and North Atlantic Current. The whole system extends beyond the Grand Banks toward the British Isles, so no 3,000 km Florida-to-Grand-Banks span is treated as its complete length.

entries.name: Gulf Stream
entries.scope: Tomczak and Godfrey report approximately 2,500 km for the Gulf Stream proper as an open-ocean free jet downstream of Cape Hatteras toward the Newfoundland Rise/Grand Banks near 50°W. This excludes the Florida Current and North Atlantic Current; it is a textbook path-scale description, not a measured reference streamline. NOAA's glossary uses the same strict segment definition, while NASA and NOAA Coast Pilot sometimes use Gulf Stream more broadly.
entries.length_source_locator: Chapter 14, The Atlantic Ocean, PDF page 11 (printed page 239), paragraph beginning Recirculation of Gulf Stream water (next 2,500 km Gulf Stream proper)

other_observations.source_locator: PDF page 3, Section 2.1 Underwater Glider Data and Methods, paragraph on 52 missions sampling a roughly 2,000 km Gulf Stream reach

entries.name: Kuroshio Current
entries.scope: Approximate Kuroshio journey from about 12°N to 35°N in the western North Pacific; not a measured whole-current axis, and the Kuroshio Extension is separate.
entries.length_source_locator: PDF page 3, Introduction opening paragraph (3,000 km journey from about 12°N to 35°N)

entries.name: Agulhas Current
entries.scope: The research description spans roughly 27°S–40°S; the coastal path is longer than its north–south separation. Retroflection, leakage, and the eastward Agulhas Return Current are distinct from this boundary-current core. The derived floor is unranked. A 2021 review also describes a roughly 1,000 km coastal segment. That narrower usage conflicts with the broader 27°S–40°S derived floor, so the two numbers are displayed as source-specific scopes and neither is ranked as a common whole-current length.
entries.length_source_locator: Section The Agulhas Current, opening paragraph (27–40°S); 1,400 km floor is OSW meridional gate geometry

source_reported_length_variants.scope: Coastal western boundary current along southeastern Africa; narrower than the 27°S–40°S span used for the existing broad lower bound. End gates and centerline are not specified.
source_reported_length_variants.source_locator: Section 2.1.1 Background, opening paragraph (1,000 km western boundary current)

entries.name: Agulhas Return Current
entries.scope: The hydrographic survey distinguishes the Agulhas Return Current from the Agulhas Current and traces its weakening eastward flow toward the Crozet Basin. This derived distance floor is not a measured streamline, whole-current length, or the length of the westward Agulhas Current.
entries.length_source_locator: PDF pages 20–22, Figure 14 and Section 6 Conclusions, Agulhas Return Current surveyed eastward from 18°E to 76°E; 3,000 km floor is OSW gate geometry

entries.name: East Australian Current
entries.scope: A derived minimum north–south span for the coherent shelf-break jet only; not a measured streamline or a published whole-current length. Separation and extension shift over time.
entries.length_source_locator: Section 1 Introduction, opening EAC paragraph (15–32°S); 1,800 km floor is OSW meridional gate geometry

entries.name: Tasman Front
entries.scope: The East Australian Current separates eastward as the Tasman Front at a variable latitude, reported between 28°S and 37°S. The cited study does not give stable whole-front endpoints or an along-flow length; do not add this branch to the East Australian Current's coastal floor. A 2019 review found the front rarely distinct in instantaneous fields; a single stable path length would overstate that evidence.

entries.name: Peru (Humboldt) Current
entries.scope: Approximate 6,000 km Humboldt Current belt from southern Chile toward northern Peru and the Galápagos, reported in an embedded Purca et al. manuscript in Purca Cuicapusa's 2005 thesis. This is a broad eastern South Pacific current-system extent, not a measured core streamline or the Peru Coastal Current alone; the manuscript separately describes its 1,000 km Peru study area.
entries.length_source_locator: PDF page 65, embedded Purca et al. manuscript, Introduction opening paragraph (ca. 6,000 km belt); PDF page 66 distinguishes its 1,000 km Peru study area

entries.name: Benguela Current
entries.scope: The study identifies the Benguela Current system at 30°, 24°, and 19°S across decadal inverse solutions, with no continuity north of 19°S. The current and Benguela ecosystem have different extents. Section observations are from different cruises and do not establish a simultaneous centerline; the derived floor is unranked.
entries.length_source_locator: Section 3.1.3 and Figure 5, Benguela Current system at 30°S, 24°S, and 19°S; OSW WGS84 meridional gate calculation

entries.name: Canary Current
entries.scope: A fall 2009 section at 29°N locates a westward extent across the section and separates transport by depth layer. It does not measure the current's along-flow length.

entries.name: Labrador Current
entries.scope: No comparable path-length estimate admitted yet.

entries.name: Greenland–Middle Atlantic shelf-current hypothesis
entries.scope: A 1989 paper hypothesizes a 5,000 km buoyancy-driven coastal connection from southern Greenland to the Middle Atlantic Bight based on limited oxygen-isotope evidence. This proposed system length is unranked and is not the length of the Labrador Current alone.
entries.length_source_locator: Abstract, proposed 5,000 km buoyancy-driven coastal current from southern Greenland to the Middle Atlantic Bight

entries.name: Brazil Current
entries.scope: The study identifies southward Brazil Current transport at 19°, 24°, and 30°S. Confluence location and downstream identity vary. Section observations are from different cruises and do not establish a simultaneous centerline; the derived floor is unranked.
entries.length_source_locator: Section 3.1.2 and Figure 5, Brazil Current at 19°S, 24°S, and 30°S; OSW WGS84 meridional gate calculation

entries.name: North Atlantic Current
entries.scope: NOAA's glossary defines this as a named Gulf Stream System segment from southeast of the Grand Banks near 40°N, 50°W toward the British Isles. Its downstream branches and whole-current path length are unresolved here.

entries.name: Deep Western Boundary Current
entries.scope: The study identifies southward deep western boundary flow at 47°, 36°, and 24.5°N in decadal inverse solutions. This is a North Atlantic segment only; sections from different cruises do not establish one simultaneous continuous path or a whole-Atlantic current length. The derived floor is unranked.
entries.length_source_locator: Section 3.2.3 and Figure 8, DWBC at 47°N, 36°N, and 24.5°N; OSW WGS84 meridional gate calculation

entries.name: Azores Current
entries.scope: The 110 km figure below is width across one 2009 meridional section at 24.5°W, not along-current length or a whole-current extent.

other_observations.source_locator: Abstract [1] and Section 4 Discussion and Conclusions [15], October 2009 section at 24.5°W; each current has 110 km meridional width

entries.name: Azores Countercurrent
entries.scope: The 110 km figure below is width across one 2009 meridional section at 24.5°W, not along-current length or a whole-current extent.

other_observations.source_locator: Abstract [1] and Section 4 Discussion and Conclusions [15], October 2009 section at 24.5°W; each current has 110 km meridional width

entries.name: Portugal Current
entries.scope: The 2009 study identifies one zonal crossing at 37°N; its 13.5–14.8°W longitude band and transport do not establish a whole-current length. Keep the offshore Portugal Current distinct from coastal counterflows.

entries.name: Mediterranean Undercurrent
entries.scope: RAFOS floats and hydrography track the undercurrent from the Gulf of Cádiz around southwestern Portugal, where a roughly 30 km wide jet weakens and broadens northward. That width is cross-stream, not its length; branching and loss from the slope prevent a single measured endpoint here.

entries.name: East Adriatic Current
entries.scope: 2002–2003 measurements off the eastern Adriatic coast establish a variable current that strengthened in January–February and again in May. Its Dalmatian coastal reach may overlap the older Dalmatian Current name, but that synonymy is not yet established; no full path length is admitted.

entries.name: Black Sea Rim Current
entries.scope: Copernicus Marine defines this basin-scale cyclonic flow and measures intensity in northern and southern slope sectors. Those sectors are monitoring windows, not a full current centerline or length. Older Caucasus and Southern Current names may describe sectors, but equivalence is unresolved.

entries.name: Loop Current
entries.scope: The loop expands and retracts; its path length changes.

entries.name: Florida Current
entries.scope: Tomczak and Godfrey report approximately 1,200 km from the Florida Straits along the coast to separation near Cape Hatteras. This is the Florida Current segment of the Gulf Stream System, not a whole-system length or a measured reference streamline. NOAA's glossary independently names the same segment; NASA and NOAA Coast Pilot sometimes use Gulf Stream more broadly for the Florida Straits flow.
entries.length_source_locator: Chapter 14, The Atlantic Ocean, PDF page 11 (printed page 239), paragraph beginning Recirculation of Gulf Stream water (1,200 km downstream to Cape Hatteras)

entries.name: North Brazil Current
entries.scope: Retroflection and rings need separate treatment.

entries.name: Alaska Current
entries.scope: No comparable path-length estimate admitted yet.

entries.name: Aleutian Current
entries.scope: The meteorological glossary identifies this as the southern eastward limb of the North Pacific subpolar gyre, also called the Subarctic Current. Its mixing with the North Pacific Current and variable frontal boundary leave no source-defined whole-current length for this ledger.

entries.name: Antilles Current
entries.scope: NOAA's six sections near 28°35′N found variable northward and southward bands rather than the broad, persistent northward surface current shown on older charts. This section cannot establish a whole-current path or length and does not resolve flow farther south.

entries.name: Davidson Current
entries.scope: A seasonal countercurrent, not a permanent jet.

entries.name: East Greenland Current
entries.scope: The study distinguishes the outer East Greenland Current from the coastal branch and assesses the system between the 78.5°N Fram Strait section and Cape Farewell. The coast-following route may be longer than the north–south separation; no comparable whole-current centerline length is admitted, so this regional floor is unranked.
entries.length_source_locator: Section 2, paragraph defining East Greenland shelf from Fram Strait 78.5°N to Cape Farewell 59°N; 2,100 km floor is OSW meridional gate geometry

entries.name: East Greenland Coastal Current
entries.scope: A summer 2004 hydrographic and velocity survey identified this inner-shelf branch along the approximately 1,000 km southeast Greenland shelf south of Denmark Strait. That is a documented regional reach, not a measured whole-current path or a year-round length; the offshore East Greenland Current is distinct.

other_observations.source_locator: PDF page 36, Conclusions opening paragraph (current along entire 1,000 km southeast Greenland shelf)

entries.name: Falkland (Malvinas) Current
entries.scope: Source-reported approximate 2,000 km northward loop of the northern Antarctic Circumpolar Current branch in the Argentine Basin, from a 2009 EGU conference abstract. No reference centerline, endpoint coordinates, depth-defined length or uncertainty is supplied. Do not interpret this as a measured dated path, a shelf-break front length, or an independently specified Malvinas Return Current extent.
entries.length_source_locator: Page 1, opening sentence of EGU2009-12242 abstract (2000 km northward loop)

entries.name: Guiana Current
entries.scope: No comparable path-length estimate admitted yet.

entries.name: Guinea Current
entries.scope: No comparable path-length estimate admitted yet.

entries.name: Irminger Current
entries.scope: No comparable path-length estimate admitted yet.

entries.name: Kuroshio Extension
entries.scope: A named continuation of the Kuroshio; keep separate from its core length.

entries.name: Monsoon Current
entries.scope: Seasonal reversal changes the path and direction.

entries.name: Indonesian Throughflow
entries.scope: NASA names the Pacific-to-Indian freshwater passage through narrow gaps of the Maritime Continent but gives no single current centerline or whole-system length. This is a multi-channel flow, so no length enters the ranking.

entries.name: Red Sea saline overflow
entries.scope: NASA identifies a saline overflow contribution from the Red Sea to the western Indian Ocean. The gateway at Bab el Mandeb is not a measured plume endpoint or a whole-flow centerline; the downstream pathway and seasonal strength require separate observations.

entries.name: Persian Gulf saline overflow
entries.scope: NASA identifies a saline overflow contribution from the Persian Gulf to the western Indian Ocean. The Strait of Hormuz gateway is not a measured plume endpoint or a whole-flow centerline; dilution and circulation beyond the strait require separate observations.

entries.name: North Cape Current
entries.scope: No comparable path-length estimate admitted yet.

entries.name: North Equatorial Current
entries.scope: The same name is used in multiple basins; split into basin-specific records before measuring.

entries.name: North Pacific Current
entries.scope: Branches and continuation limits require a declared rule.

entries.name: Norwegian Current
entries.scope: No comparable path-length estimate admitted yet. Published usage of this name overlaps with, or distinguishes it from, the Norwegian Coastal Current; identity remains unresolved here.

entries.name: Norwegian Coastal Current
entries.scope: A source identifies the current along the Norwegian coast and represents it with stations 1 and 5 nautical miles off Torungen; this is a section location, not a whole-current length. Its relation to the name Norwegian Current is convention-dependent.

entries.name: Algerian Current
entries.scope: The source describes a coastal current along Algeria that sheds mesoscale eddies; the atlas point is regional and does not define a start, end, or measured centerline.

entries.name: Balearic Current
entries.scope: The source describes a branch of the Northern Current turning near 40.6°N and contributing to flow in front of Mallorca; no comparable whole-current length is given.

entries.name: Western Adriatic Current
entries.scope: Drifter evidence identifies a fast, coastally confined southeastward flow along the Italian Adriatic coast; the regional atlas point is not a measured centerline or length endpoint.

entries.name: Baffin Current
entries.scope: The source identifies Baffin Island Current flow along western Baffin Bay; the atlas point is regional, with no source-defined whole-current centerline or length.

entries.name: Mauritanian Current
entries.scope: The source reports poleward surface flow during the May–July relaxation season in the Mauritanian upwelling region; winter upwelling-season coastal flow is equatorward. A single year-round direction or whole-current length would misrepresent this seasonal regime.

entries.name: Gaspé Current
entries.scope: The source places the jet along the Gaspé Peninsula and reports a typical width of about 10–20 km near its strongest reach; width is not along-current length, and no comparable whole-current estimate is admitted.

entries.name: Northern Current
entries.scope: The named flow is described from the Ligurian Sea along the Provençal and Catalan coasts. The cited paper reports widths and local sections, not a comparable whole-current alongstream length.

entries.name: Ligurian Current
entries.scope: The source describes a Northern Current formed in the Ligurian Sea that flows onward along the Provençal and Balearic slopes; the Ligurian name is treated here as its source-region segment, without assigning the whole system's extent to this record.

entries.name: Oyashio
entries.scope: No comparable path-length estimate admitted yet.

entries.name: Somali Current
entries.scope: Seasonal reversal makes a single static length misleading.

entries.name: South Equatorial Current
entries.scope: The same name is used in multiple basins; split into basin-specific records before measuring.

entries.name: Spitsbergen Atlantic Current
entries.scope: No comparable path-length estimate admitted yet.

entries.name: Tsushima Current
entries.scope: A segment of the Kuroshio system in NOAA's glossary.

entries.name: West Australian Current
entries.scope: No comparable path-length estimate admitted yet.

entries.name: Leeuwin Current
entries.scope: Published lower bound for southward flow along Western Australia's continental shelf, from tropical to cool-temperate coasts; distinct from the northward West Australian Current offshore. A lower bound is not a ranked whole-current estimate.
entries.length_source_locator: PDF page 108 (viewer page including cover); source states more than 2,000 km

entries.name: Western and southern Australian boundary flow
entries.scope: Continuous austral-winter shelf-edge flow from North West Cape to southern Tasmania, comprising the Leeuwin, South Australian, and Zeehan currents; not the length of Leeuwin alone.
entries.length_source_locator: Abstract [1] and Section 9 Discussion and Conclusion [53] (5,500 km winter boundary-flow system)

entries.name: South Australian Current
entries.scope: Named section from eastern Great Australian Bight to western Bass Strait in the source's winter boundary-flow convention.

entries.name: Zeehan Current
entries.scope: Named section off western Tasmania in the source's winter boundary-flow convention.

entries.name: Caribbean Current
entries.scope: No source-defined whole-current path length admitted yet.

entries.name: Equatorial Countercurrent
entries.scope: Umbrella label for multiple eastward tropical countercurrents. North and South named families and basin-specific flows require separate boundaries and length estimates.

entries.name: North Equatorial Countercurrent
entries.scope: Atlantic and Pacific upper-ocean currents share a name but have distinct paths and seasonality. The family has no single measured length; this is distinct from the deeper North Equatorial Undercurrent.

entries.name: Atlantic North Equatorial Countercurrent
entries.scope: Observed cores near 6.5°N and 8°N at 38°W in the 1998–2006 survey record, with marked seasonal variability. These cross-sections do not determine an along-current length.

entries.name: Pacific North Equatorial Countercurrent
entries.scope: Repeated Pacific velocity sections identify a near-surface eastward core around 7°N at 140°W. The section locates the current but gives no comparable along-current length.

entries.name: South Equatorial Countercurrent
entries.scope: Separate Atlantic, Pacific, and Indian eastward tropical flows share this name. Their seasonal expression and geographic limits differ; no cross-basin family length can be ranked.

entries.name: Atlantic South Equatorial Countercurrent
entries.scope: Ship observations place a weak eastward flow in the 7–9°S belt near 30°W in some seasons, with westward flow in spring 1994. The western survey limit and intermittency prevent a defensible whole-current length.

entries.name: Pacific South Equatorial Countercurrent
entries.scope: Argo-based analysis reports a boreal-spring band near 5–13°S from 150°E to 170°W, with seasonal changes in zonal reach and depth. That observed seasonal envelope is not a traced alongstream length and is unranked.

entries.name: Indian Ocean South Equatorial Countercurrent
entries.scope: Repeated XBT shipping-line sections identify this flow, including a western line near 55°E with a variable trough around 5–10°S. Section transports and latitude bands are not an along-current length.

entries.name: Equatorial Undercurrent
entries.scope: A shared subsurface name across three basins. The Indian Ocean expression is weaker and seasonal; component currents require separate boundaries and length estimates.

entries.name: Pacific Equatorial Undercurrent
entries.scope: Approximate basin-wide eastward pathway from north of Papua New Guinea to the South American coast described in Grenier et al. (2011). The source's 14,000 km is a broad path estimate, not a traced instantaneous core or the length of the Atlantic or Indian Equatorial Undercurrent. A 0°N, 140°W mooring locates the current independently.
entries.length_source_locator: Section 1 Introduction, paragraph [2] (14,000 km pathway)

source_reported_length_variants.scope: A later wave–current dynamics paper describes the Pacific EUC as traversing the equatorial Pacific over about 13,000 km. It does not define the same exact core or gates as Grenier et al.; retained as a source-specific whole-basin approximation rather than an independent rank.
source_reported_length_variants.source_locator: Introduction, opening Equatorial Undercurrent description, entire Pacific equatorial length about 13,000 km

entries.name: Atlantic Equatorial Undercurrent
entries.scope: A PIRATA ADCP observed the current at 0°N, 23°W in 2002; the station is not a whole-current length. Lomonosov is an established alternate name; Marine Regions spells it Lomonoscov.

entries.name: Indian Ocean Equatorial Undercurrent
entries.scope: Observed across a 2°S–2°N section at 90°E on 1–3 March 2017; the reported ~13.5 Sv is section transport, not path length. A later review describes the Indian expression as weaker and seasonally varying; one campaign does not establish a permanent path.

entries.name: North Equatorial Undercurrent
entries.scope: The same name is used for separately observed Atlantic and Pacific subsurface flows with different latitude and depth settings. Do not rank a cross-basin family length.

entries.name: Atlantic North Equatorial Undercurrent
entries.scope: Direct observations near 5°N, 23°W cover a 65–270 m subsurface layer; variability is dominated by intraseasonal events, and the mooring does not determine basin-wide length.

entries.name: Pacific North Equatorial Undercurrent
entries.scope: The 130°E mooring array measures eastward subsurface jets between 8.5°N and 17.5°N, with 5.1 Sv mean positive transport to 900 m under the study definition. This cross-section is not a path length.

entries.name: South Equatorial Undercurrent
entries.scope: The same name appears in separate Atlantic and Indian observations, with different vertical reach and seasonality; a family has no single measured length.

entries.name: Atlantic South Equatorial Undercurrent
entries.scope: The 35°W section identifies eastward flow between 2.5°S and 4°S at 200–500 m, with 2.8 Sv mean transport under the study definition. Section transport is not whole-current length.

entries.name: Indian Ocean South Equatorial Undercurrent
entries.scope: A 10°S, 87°E mooring and reanalysis identify a subsurface eastward jet beneath the westward South Equatorial Current; its deep reach and seasonality differ from the Atlantic flow. No comparable whole-current length is admitted.

entries.name: South Atlantic Current
entries.scope: Named basin-spanning flow in the cited study; no source-defined whole-current path length admitted yet. Cartographic crossings remain separately pending review.

entries.name: South Indian Current
entries.scope: Eastward subtropical-gyre flow near 40 degrees S in the cited study; no source-defined whole-current path length admitted. Do not conflate with the Agulhas Return Current or offshore West Australian Current. Cartographic crossings remain separately pending review.

entries.name: South Pacific Current
entries.scope: Named eastward current associated with the South Pacific subtropical front; map arrows do not measure its full length.

entries.name: West Greenland Current
entries.scope: No comparable path-length estimate admitted yet.

entries.name: West Spitsbergen Current
entries.scope: Marine Regions supplies one geographic point, not a centerline or endpoints; no comparable path-length estimate admitted yet.

entries.name: Jutland Current
entries.scope: Marine Regions supplies one geographic point, not a current boundary or endpoints; no comparable path-length estimate admitted yet.

entries.name: Mindanao Current
entries.scope: The source describes flow southward along the Philippine Islands and supply to the Indonesian Throughflow, North Equatorial Countercurrent, and Pacific Equatorial Undercurrent. It gives no whole-current alongflow length or fixed endpoint gates.

entries.name: New Guinea Coastal Undercurrent
entries.scope: The source describes northwestward flow along Papua New Guinea and through Vitiaz Strait into the Pacific Equatorial Undercurrent source region. It gives no comparable whole-current centerline length.

entries.name: New Ireland Coastal Undercurrent
entries.scope: The source describes flow along New Ireland's eastern coast, with branches joining the New Guinea Coastal Undercurrent or retroflecting toward the Pacific Equatorial Undercurrent. It gives no whole-current length.

entries.name: Solomon Island Coastal Undercurrent
entries.scope: The source schematically names this equatorward flow along the Solomon Islands and says it may feed the New Ireland Coastal Undercurrent. Its continuity and whole-current length are unresolved.

entries.name: New Guinea Coastal Current
entries.scope: Three years of moorings distinguish this upper-100 m current from the deeper New Guinea Coastal Undercurrent: it flows southeastward in boreal winter and northwestward in boreal summer. The observations do not define a whole-current alongflow length.

entries.name: Pacific North Subsurface Countercurrent
entries.scope: A Pacific section at 140°W locates this eastward jet near 4°N and 200 m; the section does not determine its complete alongflow route or length.

entries.name: Pacific South Subsurface Countercurrent
entries.scope: The Pacific 140°W section resolves two south-side branches near 4.5°S at 200 m and 7°S at 250 m. These section positions do not supply a whole-current path length or a single branch-averaged centerline.

entries.name: Hiri Current
entries.scope: The literature uses Hiri Current for the northward branch after South Equatorial Current bifurcation off northeast Australia, with variable continuation around the Gulf of Papua. No one fixed path or endpoint pair is admitted for a whole-current length.

entries.name: Alaska Coastal Current (Gulf of Alaska)
entries.scope: Stabeno et al. (2016) report an approximate 1,700 km coastal system between Seward and Samalga Pass. This is the northern Gulf of Alaska/eastern Aleutian scope, separate from the offshore Alaska Current and Alaskan Stream. It does not cover every coastal flow sharing the Alaska Coastal Current name, including Arctic usage. The paper integrates intermittent observations from 1984-2014; this extent is not a measured simultaneous reference streamline or dated footprint.
entries.length_source_locator: Accepted manuscript, PDF page 2, Abstract, lines 25-28 (~1700 km, Seward to Samalga Pass); PDF page 3, Introduction, lines 51-59 defines the regional continuity scope.

entries.name: Antarctic Slope Current
entries.scope: Review-reported upper-continental-slope system span; not a measured reference streamline or dated footprint. The Antarctic Peninsula interrupts circumpolar continuity.
entries.length_source_locator: Section 1.1 ASC Characteristics, first sentence; Figure 2 caption and following paragraph qualify continuity
